transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’m kind of scared of what I’ve been doing. Like after I eat too much, I end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up so I don’t gain weight. It’s embarrassing to say out loud.

I work around cars all day, you know, and I can fix a lot of things when something’s not running right, but this… I can’t seem to fix it. It’s gotten to where I’m worried I can’t stop.
How often do you make yourself throw up after eating?

For the past few months… at least three months, I’d say there’s barely been a week where it didn’t happen. It’s usually those late-night eating episodes, when I’m already home and everything’s quiet, and then I end up going to the bathroom after.

Some weeks it’s several times. Especially when my back’s acting up and I’m home more, because then I’m just… around the kitchen more, I guess. It feels like once it starts, I already know where it’s going, which sounds awful to say.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating, like you're eating a lot very quickly?

Yeah… yeah, that’s pretty much exactly what it feels like. Once I start on those nights, it’s like my hands just keep grabbing food even while I’m telling myself, “Lucy, knock it off,” but I don’t stop.

It’s weird, because at work I’m so used to being careful, like with tools and parts and making sure I don’t mess something up, and then at home it’s like that part of my brain just… doesn’t work. I don’t really feel back in charge until it’s already over.
Do you make yourself throw up after eating because you're afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… that’s the main reason, I think. After I eat too much, I get this panic about gaining weight, and then I end up in the bathroom making myself throw up.

It’s not like I’m proud of it. I’ll tell myself I’m not going to do it again, like when a car keeps coming back with the same problem and you swear you fixed it, but then there it is again. And I get scared because it feels like I can’t stop once that thought gets in my head.
Are there times when you eat a lot very quickly and feel like you've lost control, but you don't make yourself throw up afterwards?

I mean… most of the time if I get to that point, where I’ve eaten too much and I feel out of control, I end up making myself throw up. That’s kind of why I’m here, honestly.

It’s like I’ll go into the bathroom because I’m scared I’m going to gain weight, and then I do it, even though part of me is thinking, “What are you doing?” I don’t know… I can change brakes and deal with a busted transmission, but I can’t seem to stop myself from doing that, and that scares me.
Are there times when you eat a lot very quickly and feel like you've lost control, but you don't make yourself throw up afterwards, even if it's just once in a while?

I guess… if I’m being honest, it’s mostly the same pattern. I eat too much, and then I’m in the bathroom making myself throw up because I’m scared I’ll gain weight. That’s kind of why I’m here.

I keep thinking I should be able to just stop, like when you know a bolt is stripped and you still keep trying to force it even though it’s making it worse… sorry, that’s probably not the point. But no, I don’t really have many times where I just leave it alone after. It’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it.
How many times a week do you have these episodes of eating a lot very quickly and feeling like you've lost control?

It’s… it’s been happening pretty much every week. For at least the last three months, I don’t think there’s really been a week where I didn’t have one of those late-night times where I eat fast and feel like I can’t stop, and then I go make myself throw up after.

Some weeks it’s more than once—several times, especially if I’m home more because my back’s acting up. When I’m stuck around the house, it’s like there’s too much time and I end up in that same stupid routine.
Do you make yourself throw up after every episode of eating a lot very quickly and feeling like you've lost control?

Yeah… pretty much. I mean, that’s the part that scares me. After I eat too much and feel like I’ve lost control, I usually end up in the bathroom making myself throw up because I’m terrified I’m going to gain weight.

It’s like this stupid routine now, and I hate saying that out loud. I’ll tell myself I won’t do it, like when I swear I’m not going to stay late at the shop fixing something that isn’t even my job, and then there I am anyway… sorry. But yeah, that’s why I’m here. It’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop.
Is there ever a time when you eat a lot very quickly and feel like you've lost control, but you don't make yourself throw up afterwards?

Not really… I mean, I know I kind of already said it, but that’s the whole reason I’m here. After I eat too much like that, I end up in the bathroom making myself throw up because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

I’ll tell myself, “Just don’t do it this time,” but then it’s like when a car starts pulling hard to one side and you know something’s off—you can’t just ignore it. My head just locks onto it. So… no, there really isn’t much of a time where I don’t. It’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop.
Do you ever have episodes of eating a lot very quickly and feeling like you've lost control without making yourself throw up afterwards?

No… I mean, that’s what I’m trying to say. When I have one of those times where I eat too much and I feel like I can’t stop, I end up making myself throw up after. I go to the bathroom because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

It’s embarrassing. I keep thinking of it like when a car has the same problem over and over and you tell yourself, “Okay, I know how to fix this,” but then it keeps coming back anyway. Except this is me, and I’m scared because I can’t seem to stop doing it.
Do you always make yourself throw up after eating a lot very quickly and feeling like you've lost control?

Yeah… I mean, pretty much always. That’s why I came in. After I eat too much and it feels like I can’t stop, I end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up because I’m so scared I’ll gain weight.

I know I’ve said that already, sorry. It’s just… it gets stuck in my head, like when you hear a weird noise in an engine and you can’t focus on anything else until you check it. Except with this, I’m the one doing it, and it’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop.
Do you ever eat a lot very quickly without feeling like you've lost control?

No… not really. Once I start on those nights, it’s like my hands just keep grabbing food even while I’m telling myself, “Lucy, knock it off.” Like I can see it happening but I can’t get myself to stop.

It’s kind of like when I’m working on a car and one bolt leads to another problem and then another, and suddenly the whole job got away from me—but, sorry, I know that’s not what you asked. I just mean… I don’t feel back in charge until it’s already done.
Do you ever eat a lot very quickly and then not make yourself throw up?

Not really… I mean, that’s the whole reason I’m here. When I eat too much like that, I end up in the bathroom making myself throw up because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

And I know I keep circling back to that, but it’s like at work when a problem keeps coming back no matter how many times you think you fixed it. I tell myself I won’t do it, and then after I eat, there I am again… and it scares me that I can’t seem to stop.
Is your fear of gaining weight the only reason you make yourself throw up after eating too much?

Yeah… I mean, the weight thing is the big reason. After I eat too much, I go make myself throw up in the bathroom because I’m scared of gaining weight.

But it’s also like… once that thought gets in my head, I can’t leave it alone. Like at work, if I know something’s wrong under the hood, I can’t just close it and walk away—I keep messing with it until I feel like I did something. Except this isn’t fixing anything. It’s just gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short time without then making yourself throw up?

No… not really. If I eat a lot in a short time, I almost always end up in the bathroom after, making myself throw up because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

That’s kind of why I’m here. It’s like… I know I’ve said it already, but it’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it. Like once the eating happens, my brain goes straight to, “You have to fix this,” and then I’m in there.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food without feeling like you've lost control?

No… I mean, when it happens, it doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it normally. Once I start on those nights, my hands just keep grabbing food even while I’m telling myself, “Lucy, knock it off.”

It’s kind of like when I’m working on a car and I know I should stop before I make the bolt worse, but I keep going anyway—except this is food, and I don’t feel back in charge until it’s already over.
Do you ever eat a lot very quickly without then making yourself throw up?

Not really… I mean, it usually goes the same way. If I eat too much, especially fast, I end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

I know I keep saying that, but that’s the part that scares me. It’s like when a customer keeps coming back with the same warning light and you think, “Okay, something’s really wrong here.” I keep doing it, and I’m scared I can’t stop.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short time without then making yourself throw up?

No… not really. I know I’ve kind of answered that, but if I eat too much in a short time, I pretty much end up making myself throw up after. I go to the bathroom because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

It’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it. Like at work, if something keeps happening over and over, you start thinking it’s not just a fluke, you know? That’s what this feels like.

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because after I eat too much, I keep making myself throw up in the bathroom so I won’t gain weight, and it’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether large eating episodes occur without subsequent self-induced vomiting, so the most direct topic is purging as a compensatory behavior.

patient.answer:
No… not really. I know I’ve kind of answered that, but if I eat too much in a short time, I pretty much end up making myself throw up after. I go to the bathroom because I’m scared I’ll gain weight.

It’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it. Like at work, if something keeps happening over and over, you start thinking it’s not just a fluke, you know? That’s what this feels like.

inference.note: F50.0 was ruled out as the patient's behavior is more consistent with bulimia nervosa, characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of recurrent episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short time, feeling a lack of control during these episodes, and regularly engaging in self-induced vomiting to prevent weight gain meet the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa.
